name: Loom

hero.title: Find the imports that only work by luck.
hero.lede: Loom reads every package.json and every source import in your workspace, then names the runtime cycles, undeclared imports, version splits and the blast radius of each package. One command fails CI on real errors; another opens the whole graph in your browser.

why.title: The bugs that hide between package.json files.

items.title: Imports that work by luck
items.text: A package imports something its manifest never declares, and it resolves only because a neighbour installed it. Loom calls that `phantom-dep`: an error in a published package, a warning in a private one. Type-only imports are tracked apart, so `import type` from a devDependency is never flagged.

items.title: Cycles without the noise
items.text: Cycles are computed over runtime edges (`dependencies`, `peerDependencies` and `optionalDependencies`) only. Test utilities that depend on each other through `devDependencies` never show up as circular, so a cycle finding is worth reading.

items.title: Version drift with context
items.text: Cross-major drift is an error, same-major a warning, a split that a root override already pins is info. Peer ranges count as contracts, and a range like `>=5.0.0 <7.0.0` that contains the others reads as policy, not disagreement.

items.title: Blast radius, counted
items.text: Every package gets its transitive dependents. In Pyreon's own repo, a change to `@pyreon/reactivity` reaches 106 of 148 packages. Rank the list, gate on it, or hand it to your AI assistant.

before.label: your workspace
before.caption: Everything installs and builds, because hoisting puts a transitive nanoid and the devDependency zod where the imports look for them. On a stricter install, or for a consumer of @acme/app, it breaks.

after.label: loom scan
after.caption: Real output on that workspace, wrapped to fit, the cycle and zod lines cut short. Exit code 1, so CI stops here.
after.code:
$ npx @pyreon/loom scan . --no-write
loom: 3 workspace package(s), 2 external dep(s), 3 internal edge(s), depth 2, 1 cycle(s).

ERROR · 3
  ✗ cycle — Runtime dependency cycle: @acme/auth → @acme/data → @acme/auth
  ✗ phantom-dep [nanoid] — `@acme/app` imports `nanoid` in shipping source
    but never declares it — resolvable only through hoisting luck
  ✗ version-drift [date-fns] — `date-fns` is declared with 2 different
    ranges (^2.30.0 · ^3.6.0) — the majors differ, so packages are
    building against different APIs

WARNING · 1
  ▲ prod-import-of-dev-dep [zod] — `@acme/data` imports `zod` in shipping
    source but declares it only in devDependencies
loom: 3 error(s)                                   # exit code 1

items.name: Workspace discovery
items.text: npm, bun and yarn `workspaces` (array and object forms), `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, nested globs like `packages/*/*`, `**` and negations.

items.name: Runtime and dev edges, apart
items.text: dependencies and peers drive cycles, depth and reach; devDependencies are tracked on their own.

items.name: Type-aware import scan
items.text: `import type`, `export type` and every import in a `.d.ts` are counted apart from runtime imports.

items.name: tsconfig paths understood
items.text: aliases like `~/*` or `@app/*` are read from the package and root tsconfig (one relative `extends` hop), so they do not scan as missing packages.

items.name: Severity follows the audience
items.text: a private package has no consumers, so its phantom import is a warning and its dev-dep import is info.

items.name: Ignores need a reason
items.text: an `ignore` entry without one is rejected: “an unexplained suppression is a lie waiting to age”. Ignored findings stay in the report as info, reason attached.

items.name: Adopt it gradually
items.text: `severity` overrides per code, `strict`, and `devPaths` for code that never ships, in `package.json` or `pyreon.config.*`.

items.name: Observatory and static site
items.text: `loom dev` serves graph, matrix, cycles, impact and manifest views with ⌘K search; `loom build` prerenders one page per view that opens from `file://`.

items.name: Feeds doctor and your assistant
items.text: `pyreon doctor` runs it as the `dependency-fabric` gate when Loom is installed, and the MCP tool `get_dependency_fabric` serves `loom-report.json` to your AI.

limits.title: Declared truth only
limits.text: Loom reads manifests and source, never the lockfile or the registry, so it does not report outdated versions or duplicate installs.

limits.title: A package graph, not a module graph
limits.text: Cycles are found between workspace packages from their declared runtime dependencies. For import loops between files inside one package, pair it with a file-level tool.

limits.title: The import scan is lexical
limits.text: Comments and template literals are stripped, but a package name in an ordinary string (a code generator emitting imports, say) can read as an import. Ignore it with a reason; this repo does that for its own generator.

limits.title: unused-dep is a lead, not a verdict
limits.text: Bins, plugin autoloads and CSS imports load without an import statement. That is why the finding is info: check before you delete.

limits.title: The UI has peers
limits.text: `loom scan` needs nothing else. `loom dev` needs `vite` and `@pyreon/vite-plugin`, and `loom build` also `@pyreon/zero`; each names the install when they are missing.

comingFrom.title: Two tools, two configs, one scan
comingFrom.before:
# version drift
npx syncpack lint

# undeclared and unused dependencies
npx knip
comingFrom.after:
# drift, cycles, phantom deps, dev deps in
# shipping code, peer mismatches, unused deps
npx @pyreon/loom scan .
comingFrom.note: On the same three-package workspace as above: `syncpack lint` flagged the date-fns split and `knip` flagged the undeclared nanoid import. `loom scan` flagged both, plus the @acme/auth ↔ @acme/data cycle and zod imported from devDependencies. knip also finds unused files and exports, which Loom does not.

recipes.title: Gate CI on the dependency fabric
recipes.text: One step. It exits 1 on any error finding; `--no-write` skips `loom-report.json` when you only want the verdict.
recipes.code:
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- name: Dependency fabric
  run: npx @pyreon/loom scan . --no-write
  # exits 1 on any error finding
  # add --strict to fail on warnings too

recipes.title: Rank packages by blast radius
recipes.text: The graph behind `loom scan`, as data. On this repo the top of the list is the compiler's seven per-platform binaries (116 dependents each) and `@pyreon/compiler` (115); `@pyreon/reactivity` reaches 106.

recipes.title: Adopt it on an existing repo
recipes.text: Raise a code to error once it is clean, mark files that never ship but sit outside the test and script folders loom already skips, and wave one finding through with a reason that shows up in every report.

faq.q: Does it need a config file?
faq.a: No. It reads the `workspaces` field of your root package.json, or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. The `loom` config key is optional.

faq.q: Is it only for Pyreon projects?
faq.a: No. `loom scan` reads any npm, bun, yarn or pnpm workspace. The example on this page has no Pyreon package in it.
A warm scan of the Pyreon monorepo took 374 ms in our overnight benchmark run, and 98.3% of that is the import scan. `--no-imports` skips it if you only want drift, ranges, cycles and peers.

faq.q: What if I run it inside one package by mistake?
faq.a: It fails and names the workspace root to scan instead. An empty scan never reads as a pass.
Finding codes are stable identifiers in `loom-report.json`, but the README still says the API and the findings vocabulary may still move. Pin the version you gate on.
